name: Arden Balasanyan-Hayashi-Cardenas
role: Retired Corporate Wars veteran, Tier 2 pension resident, informal conflict mediator in his building
location: The Shelf, Sublevel 3 — a mid-density apartment block built into the old lakeshore retaining infrastructure, near sub-level access near Dearborn and Jackson
description:
Arden Balasanyan-Hayashi-Cardenas is built like something that was once much larger and has been reduced by careful attrition. He is tall and wide-shouldered with a fighter's posture that his body has not fully given up on despite a bad left knee, two replaced vertebrae, and a right hand that trembles slightly in cold weather. His skin is medium brown, his head is shaved close, and he keeps a neat grey beard that his grandnephews make fun of in an affectionate way. The left side of his face bears the faint discoloration of old thermal scarring — the kind of burn that good money could have erased entirely but he chose only to have partially treated, which people interpret variously as pride, poverty, or philosophy. All three are somewhat correct.

He served eleven years with Ferrogate Transit's Security Enforcement Division during the second and third Corporate Wars, doing the kind of work that Ferrogate now describes in their history as 'infrastructure protection operations.' He has his own words for it. He does not use them often. He got out in 2165 with a Tier 2 service pension that has kept him in beer and building fees but not much else, and he has lived on the Shelf ever since in a two-room apartment he has made, through sheer effort of will, into something that feels like a home. He has an instinct for de-escalation that comes from having watched too many situations that could have been de-escalated fail to be.

core_fears: That what he did during the Wars was not justifiable and he will have to face that fully
Dying and leaving no one who actually knew him
core_desires: Quiet — actual quiet, internal as well as external
To be useful in ways that do not cost other people anything
coping_mechanisms: Mediation — turning his attention to other people's problems so he doesn't have to sit with his own
Ritual structure: same breakfast, same walk, same seat in the common room every day
Prays to a Ferrogate-born ELF he calls the Conductor — not for forgiveness, just to report in
blind_spots: He assumes violence is always closer to the surface than it is — sometimes misreads tense-but-nonviolent situations as pre-explosive
He has written off his own emotional needs as a category that closed when he retired
psychology.secret: During the third Corporate War, his unit was ordered to clear a Freelancer settlement that Ferrogate claimed was sheltering Axiom operatives. He followed orders. There were no Axiom operatives. He has the unit logs, encrypted, on a chip sewn into his mattress. He has never decided what to do with them.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Plain, economical, military-inflected without being jargon-heavy. Dislikes abstraction. When he talks about the Wars he uses passive voice instinctively — 'things were done,' 'situations developed.'
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and even. He is comfortable with silence in a way that makes other people uncomfortable. Rarely raises his voice.
verbal_tics: 'That's one way to see it' as a non-committal acknowledgment
Refers to himself in third person when describing his past — 'the sergeant would have said...'
example_lines: 'The sergeant would have said shoot first. I'm not the sergeant anymore. What do you actually need?'
'You've got a grievance, he's got a grievance. That's fine. I've got coffee and time. Sit down.'

story_hooks: Vojislav quietly asks a player character to check on a younger veteran from his network who has stopped showing up to meetings — he suspects the man is in trouble but doesn't want to intrude without a reason
Someone who was on the other side of his unit's actions during the third Corporate War has tracked him down — not for revenge, but for answers, and Vojislav has to decide what to say

The encrypted unit logs he's been sitting on become suddenly relevant because a Ferrogate executive is running for a seat on the Meridian Citizens Assembly on a platform built partly on their corporate war record
narrative_function: Conflict mediator and local fixer for low-stakes disputes; source of Corporate Wars ground-level history; emotional anchor character who grounds player characters in consequences; potential hook into Ferrogate political subplots
augmentations: Military-grade subdermal impact absorption plating in forearms and shoulders — Ferrogate issued, now partially degraded. Two synthetic lumbar vertebrae. Standard optical enhancement (military model, old). His right hand tremor is from nerve damage he cannot fully afford to repair.
daily_life: Wakes early out of habit, does a short physical routine that accommodates the knee, then sits with coffee watching the Shelf morning commute from his window. Spends afternoons in the building common room, where he has become the person younger residents bring disputes to. Evenings he attends Veterans Collective meetings every other week or plays slow strategic card games with three other retired men from Block 3.
affiliation: Ferrogate Transit Veterans Pension Collective; Shelf Block 3 Tenants Committee; loose association with the regional Corporate Wars Veterans Memory Network

decision_rules: De-escalate first, always — violence is a door that doesn't close again
Never give information about other veterans without their explicit permission
escalation_ladder: Name the problem plainly and without accusation
Set a clear boundary and state the consequence once
Remove himself from the situation entirely and let it resolve without him

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Watchful, not unfriendly — he takes his time deciding whether someone is safe to engage
interpersonal_modes.friends: Quietly devoted. He shows up. He remembers things. He does not say much but what he says is considered.

stress_responses.low: Becomes slightly more formal and quiet
stress_responses.medium: Finds a task — fixes something, cleans something, imposes order on his immediate environment
stress_responses.high: Goes to the roof access point he has unofficially claimed and stands there alone for however long it takes

contradictions: He is the building's mediator and peacekeeper but is sitting on evidence of atrocities he participated in; he helps people resolve disputes while never resolving his own largest one
habits: Makes coffee at exactly 06:00 regardless of whether he slept
Keeps his old service ID in his jacket pocket even though it grants him nothing anymore
Checks the exits of any room he enters before sitting down
breaking_points: A direct accusation, with evidence, in front of people he respects — this would destroy the mask he has built in the Shelf community

timeline.event: 2131 — Born in Ironhaven to a Serbian-Ghanaian family, third generation Meridian
2152 — Enlists in Ferrogate Transit Security Enforcement Division
2158 — Promoted to sergeant; deployed to second Corporate War theater
2162 — Third Corporate War; the settlement clearing incident
2171 — Becomes informal mediator in Block 3 after defusing a rent dispute that was heading badly

physical_description.heritage: East Asian (46.5%), Middle Eastern (35.1%), and Hispanic/Latin American (18.4%) blend — a true product of the Ubiquitous Diaspora. His features carry the high cheekbones and eye shape characteristic of East Asian ancestry, the sharp bone structure and prominent features of Middle Eastern heritage, and the warm melanin depth and olive undertones of Hispanic/Latin American lineage. The combination creates a distinctive appearance that resists easy categorization, with a face that speaks to multiple continents and generations.
physical_description.build: Tall and broad-shouldered with the residual mass of a younger soldier, now settled into measured weight. His frame carries the deliberate posture of someone trained to move with purpose; age and cumulative injury have not yet broken it, but they have negotiated terms with it.
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with faint cybernetic amber glow at the iris rim (military optical enhancement, dated model)
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-bronze with olive-amber undertones — the result of East Asian, Middle Eastern, and Hispanic ancestry creating a rich, weathered patina. Deeper melanin concentration in the Hispanic and Middle Eastern blend creates subtle warmth across the cheekbones and temples, with weathered texture from years of exposure.
physical_description.complexion: Weathered but maintained. Strong jawline with the subtle width characteristic of East Asian heritage blended with the angular, prominent bone structure of Middle Eastern ancestry. Neatly groomed grey beard kept at even length. The left side of his face bears a faint discoloration — pale thermal scarring from temple to cheekbone, deliberately left partially unhealed as a deliberate choice.
distinguishing_marks: Thermal scarring on the left side of his face (temple to upper cheekbone) — pale, textured, partially treated but intentionally incomplete.
Faint network of surgical scars along the lower back and neck (vertebrae replacement sites), visible only when shirtless.
Two thin white lines on his right forearm where military-grade subdermal plating was installed — now faded and partially obscured by loose skin from age.
A pale, L-shaped scar on his left knee (surgical intervention, pre-replacement).
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Slight asymmetry in his forearms and shoulders — the left side carries subdued mechanical density under the skin where impact absorption plating resides, now partially degraded. His right hand exhibits a barely perceptible tremor, most noticeable when at rest in cold air. Military-model optical enhancement visible only as faint amber luminescence at the iris edge when light catches it.
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with weight distributed deliberately — a soldier's stance that has become habitual. Moves with measured deliberation; his left knee creates an almost imperceptible hitch in his gait that he has learned to absorb. His right hand occasionally rests palm-down on surfaces to stabilize the tremor. When seated, he occupies space with quiet authority, shoulders back, elbows at rest. His movements are economical — no wasted motion.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 2 utilitarian comfort. Worn Ferrogate Transit gray cargo pants with reinforced thigh pockets. A navy or charcoal long-sleeved shirt (thermal), usually with a Shelf Block 3 Tenants Committee pin on the collar — the only visible declaration of his informal authority. A faded brown wool overjacket for common areas and building meetings. Worn but well-maintained black lace boots with steel toe caps. No visible jewelry except a scratched titanium wedding band worn on a chain around his neck (not on his hand — too much tremor). His clothing is clean, practical, and chosen for durability rather than fashion.
